paper_metadata.title: High-temperature corrosion behavior of Inconel 617 with Ni-claddings in molten FLiNaK salt

evidence.quote: Inconel 617 exhibits obvious intergranular corrosion in molten FLiNaK salt with high Ni 2+ concentration, which is attributed to the dissolution of Cr, Co, and formed ions in the salt.

Ni ‐claddings exhibit much more excellent corrosion resistance than the Inconel 617, and the high ‐temperature corrosion resistance of the Inconel 617 can be significantly improved by the Ni ‐claddings.

evidence.section: 4.2 | Galvanic corrosion between 617 alloys and Ni ‐claddings
evidence.quote: It should be noted that Ni ‐617 shows much more severe corrosion than 617 alloys without Ni ‐claddings, indicating much more severe corrosion could happen if Ni ‐claddings were broken in the molten FLiNaK salts.

phases_and_microstructures.name: Cr- and Co-depleted, Fe- and Ni-rich near-surface layer

attributes.composition: Cr- and Co-depleted, Fe- and Ni-rich

evidence.quote: Cr and Co can continuously transfer into the molten salts, leaving numerous va- cancies behind, resulting in a Cr ‐ and Co ‐depleted and Fe‐ and Ni ‐rich layer on the near ‐surface of Inconel 617 (Figure 4d,g,j,m).
Inconel 617 exhibits obvious intergranular corrosion in molten FLiNaK salt with high Ni 2+ concentration, which is attributed to the dissolution of Cr, Co, and formed ions in the salt.

If the Ni ‐cladding is broken, the interactions of the Inconel 617 and the Ni ‐claddings can increase the intergranular corrosion of base 617 alloys and induce a mass transfer of Co from Inconel 617 to Ni ‐claddings through the molten salt.

evidence.section: 4.2 | Galvanic corrosion between 617 alloys and Ni ‐claddings
evidence.quote: For the Ni‐617 specimen, a galvanic couple between Inconel 617 and Ni ‐claddings formed. The Ni ‐claddings work as the cathode because the corrosion ‐resistant Ni is its main component and the Ni ‐claddings have a much lower Cr concentration than the Inconel 617.

evidence.section: 4.2 | Galvanic corrosion between 617 alloys and Ni ‐claddings
evidence.quote: the dissolved Co ions in the salts are transferred to the Ni ‐claddings, where they are reduced to Co atoms and alloyed with the Ni ‐claddings. This process is accelerated by the variation in the activity of Co in the two galvanic combined alloys, which continuously stimulate corrosion even after the original oxidants in the salts are consumed.

Due to the redox reaction of Fe 2+ and Ni 2+ with Cr and Co on the surface of the alloys as described in Equations ( 1), ( 2), and ( 4), Cr and Co can continuously transfer into the molten salts, leaving numerous va- cancies behind
resulting in a Cr ‐ and Co ‐depleted and Fe‐ and Ni ‐rich layer on the near ‐surface of Inconel 617 (Figure 4d,g,j,m).
